act_title: The Patents Act, 1970 (as amended up to Patents Rules 2024)
authority: Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), Ministry of Commerce and Industry
version_tag: Act 39 of 1970 as amended by Act 15 of 2005 and Patents (Amendment) Rules, 2024

sections.heading: Inventions relating to Traditional Knowledge not patentable
sections.text: The following are not inventions within the meaning of this Act: (p) an invention which in effect, is traditional knowledge or which is an aggregation or duplication of known properties of traditionally known component or components.
sections.explanation: Explicitly bars product patenting of traditional Ayurvedic formulations, classical herb mixtures, and aggregation of known medicinal attributes of plants.
sections.gazette_ref: Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Sec. 1

sections.heading: Mere discovery of a new form of a known substance without enhanced efficacy
sections.text: The following are not inventions within the meaning of this Act: (d) the mere discovery of a new form of a known substance which does not result in the enhancement of the known efficacy of that substance or the mere discovery of any new property or new use for a known substance or of the mere use of a known process, machine or apparatus unless such known process results in a new product or employs at least one new reactant.
sections.explanation: Requires clear, quantifiable demonstration of enhanced therapeutic efficacy or synergistic bio-availability for derivative formulations.
sections.gazette_ref: Novartis AG v. Union of India (2013) 6 SCC 1

sections.heading: Mere admixture resulting only in aggregation of properties
sections.text: The following are not inventions within the meaning of this Act: (e) a substance obtained by a mere admixture resulting only in the aggregation of the properties of the components thereof or a process for producing such substance.
sections.explanation: Physical mixing of known Ayurvedic herbs is unpatentable unless synergistic effect (greater than the sum of individual components) is proven with experimental data.
sections.gazette_ref: CGPDTM Guidelines for Examination of Patent Applications (Ayurveda)

sections.heading: Method of agriculture or horticulture not patentable
sections.text: The following are not inventions within the meaning of this Act: (h) a method of agriculture or horticulture.
sections.explanation: Cultivation and harvesting protocols for medicinal herbs are non-patentable subject matter in India; consider Plant Variety Protection (PPV&FR Act 2001) instead.
sections.gazette_ref: Manual of Patent Office Practice and Procedure 2019

sections.heading: Mandatory disclosure of biological material source and geographical origin
sections.text: Every complete specification shall disclose the source and geographical origin of the biological material in the specification when used in an invention.
sections.explanation: Requires complete disclosure of origin of Indian medicinal plants and biological samples used in the formulation. Failure to disclose triggers pre-grant opposition under Section 25(1)(j) or revocation under Section 64(1)(p).

act_title: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (as amended by the Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023)
authority: National Biodiversity Authority (NBA), Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
version_tag: Act 18 of 2003 as amended by Act 10 of 2023

sections.heading: Prior Approval of National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) for IPR
sections.text: No person shall apply for any intellectual property right, by whatever name called, in or outside India for any invention based on any research or information on a biological resource obtained from India without obtaining the previous approval of the National Biodiversity Authority before making such application.
sections.explanation: Strict mandatory requirement for prior NBA approval (Form III) before applying for patents using Indian medicinal herbs or biological materials. For PCT international filings, approval must precede foreign national phase entry.

sections.heading: Certain persons not to undertake Biodiversity related activities without NBA permission
sections.text: No person who is not a citizen of India, or a body corporate, association or organisation not incorporated or registered in India shall obtain any biological resource occurring in India or knowledge associated thereto for research or for commercial utilisation without prior approval of National Biodiversity Authority.
sections.explanation: Foreign entities, NRI individuals, or Indian companies with foreign equity/management utilizing Indian Ayurvedic knowledge or plants must obtain prior NBA approval under Form I.

sections.heading: Prior intimation to State Biodiversity Board (SBB) for Indian citizens
sections.text: No person who is a citizen of India or a body corporate shall obtain any biological resource for commercial utilisation or bio-survey without prior intimation to the concerned State Biodiversity Board, subject to exemptions under the amended Act.
sections.explanation: Indian citizens commercializing ASU formulations must notify the relevant State Biodiversity Board unless utilizing codified traditional knowledge strictly within domestic AYUSH channels.

act_title: WIPO Treaty on Intellectual Property, Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge (2024)

sections.heading: Mandatory Disclosure Requirement in Patent Applications
sections.text: Where the claimed invention in a patent application is materially/directly based on genetic resources or associated traditional knowledge, each Contracting Party shall require applicants to disclose the country of origin of the genetic resources or the Indigenous Peoples or local community providing the traditional knowledge.
sections.explanation: Introduces a binding international disclosure obligation across global patent offices (USPTO, EPO, JPO, WIPO PCT) for inventions originating from traditional knowledge systems like Ayurveda.

sections.heading: Non-retroactivity and Information Systems for Prior Art
sections.text: Contracting Parties shall establish information systems (databases) of genetic resources and traditional knowledge, accessible to patent examiners to prevent wrongful grant of patents.
sections.explanation: Formally integrates TKDL-style classical prior-art databases into international examination guidelines across all member states.

act_title: Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 & Rules 1945 (AYUSH Provisions)
authority: Ministry of Ayush & Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO)
version_tag: Rules 1945 as amended up to Drugs and Cosmetics (Amendment) Rules, 2023

sections.heading: Proof of effectiveness of Ayurvedic, Siddha and Unani drugs
sections.text: For the grant of manufacturing license for Ayurvedic, Siddha or Unani drugs, proof of effectiveness as prescribed in official pharmacopoeias or clinical trials shall be submitted to the State Licensing Authority.
sections.explanation: Regulatory requirement for commercial sale of ASU drugs; classical formulations in AFI/API require manufacturing license, while patent/proprietary ASU medicines require safety & efficacy proof.

sections.heading: Guidelines for Issue of License for Patent or Proprietary Ayurvedic Medicines
sections.text: Every application for license to manufacture patent or proprietary Ayurvedic, Siddha or Unani medicine shall provide pilot clinical trial data and published literature proving synergistic efficacy beyond classical formulations.
sections.explanation: Direct regulatory nexus to Section 3(e) of Patents Act: proprietary AYUSH medicines require proof of synergy and non-toxicity before marketing.

sections.heading: Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) for Ayurvedic, Siddha and Unani Medicines
sections.text: Factory premises, hygienic conditions, equipment, and quality control requirements for manufacturing ASU medicines.
sections.explanation: Mandatory manufacturing standards required before commercial distribution of any Ayurvedic formulation.
